documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonary Medicine Follow-up
Date of service: 02/05/2025

Interval history: Mr. Mayhew, 46, with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, hypertension and GERD, last seen here in June 2024 (initial evaluation February 2024, our consultation April 2024). Over the past six months his breathlessness with exertion and his dry cough have continued to creep up slowly. No travel, no sick contacts. He again raised the question of his lung cancer risk given his smoking history and current symptoms.

Current medications: nintedanib 150 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2018. Works construction.

Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air.
Lungs: bilateral end-inspiratory crackles.

Imaging today: chest x-ray with diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates. HRCT with honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis; no mass or nodule.
PFTs: restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity.
Liver tests on treatment have all been normal.

Assessment: IPF with slow symptomatic progression, resting saturation unchanged at 94%. Continue nintedanib 150 mg twice daily. On cancer risk, we explained that his CT surveillance is already looking at the lungs closely and today shows no mass or nodule.

Plan: continue nintedanib, liver tests every 3 months, reflux treatment to continue, return in 12 months with chest imaging and PFTs.

Pulmonary Medicine

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. Reviewed the Feb pulmonology letter together: IPF slowly progressing by symptoms, CT without any mass, sat unchanged, staying on nintedanib, next visit there in a year. He says the cough is the most annoying part. Taking all three meds. Reflux fine.

BP as charted, at his usual. SpO2 94% RA. Bibasilar crackles. Heart RRR. No edema.

A/P: HTN, continue HCTZ 25, BMP today. GERD, continue omeprazole 20. IPF per pulmonology. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, pushed back from the fall at his request. Turns 48 in a couple of weeks. IPF on nintedanib since 4/2024, followed by pulmonology yearly with quarterly LFTs (all normal); next pulmonology visit later this month. Breathing with exertion unchanged from his last visit here, dry cough persists, no fevers. BP pill and reflux pill daily. Off tobacco seven years. Drinks rarely. Mood fine, PHQ-2 0.

Meds: nintedanib 150 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily. No drug allergies.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 94% RA. Well appearing, speaking in full sentences. HEENT normal. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur, no gallop. Lungs: fine crackles at both bases, unchanged. Abdomen soft, nontender. No clubbing or edema. Skin clear.

A/P:
1. IPF: stable at rest; pulmonology visit 2/17.
2. HTN: at baseline on HCTZ 25. CMP.
3. GERD: controlled, continue omeprazole 20.
4. Prevention: CBC, lipids, A1c. FIT kit given (missed doing one in the fall). Flu and COVID done in October, PCV20 2024.
Follow up in about 6 months.

Pulmonary Medicine Follow-up
Date of service: 02/17/2026

Mr. Mayhew is a 47-year-old man with hypertension and gastroesophageal reflux disease followed here for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis since 2024. He returns for his yearly review. Exertional breathlessness and a nonproductive cough continue to progress. He has not traveled and has had no sick contacts.

Medications: nintedanib 150 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known.
Social: former smoker, 30 pack-years. Continues to work in construction.

Exam: SpO2 94% on room air. Bilateral end-inspiratory crackles.

Studies today: chest x-ray, diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates. HRCT, subpleural reticular change and honeycombing with no significant lymphadenopathy. PFTs, restrictive with reduced diffusion capacity. Quarterly liver tests on nintedanib normal.

Impression and plan: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Continue nintedanib 150 mg twice daily, liver tests every 3 months, continue reflux management, return in 12 months or sooner with any change.
